schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE USER (UID INT, UNAME INT, CITY INT);
CREATE TABLE PICTURE (UID INT, SIZE INT);
q1: SELECT P.UID, P.UNAME, COALESCE(Q.CNT, 0) AS CNT FROM (SELECT X.UID, X.UNAME FROM USER AS X WHERE X.CITY = 3) AS P LEFT JOIN (SELECT Y.UID, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM PICTURE AS Y WHERE Y.SIZE > 1000000 GROUP BY Y.UID) AS Q USING (UID)
q2: SELECT X.UID AS UID, X.UNAME AS UNAME, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM USER AS X, PICTURE AS Y WHERE X.UID = Y.UID AND Y.SIZE > 1000000 AND X.CITY = 3 GROUP BY X.UID, X.UNAME

explanation: Q1 uses a LEFT JOIN, including users from CITY=3 even if they have no qualifying pictures (CNT=0). Q2 uses an INNER JOIN, excluding users with no qualifying pictures. The difference arises when users in CITY=3 have no pictures over 1MB.
counterexample_dsp: User 1 is in CITY=3 with no pictures. User 2 is in CITY=3 with one picture under 1MB. Q1 includes both users (with CNT=0 for both), while Q2 excludes both due to no qualifying pictures.
